concerns.location: plan.md: Phase 3 / Phase 6; research.md Methodology items 3, 6
concerns.text: The plan builds a stratified 80/10/10 train/val/test split (FR-004) but then evaluates via 5-fold CV 'on the training portion' and reports CV means as the headline metrics. The role of the held-out 10% test set is never stated — is it used for final reporting, for the RF comparison, or discarded? If final metrics are CV means, the test split is dead weight and the FR-006 'shared test set' comparison is replaced by CV-fold pairing without a truly untouched evaluation set. Specify which artifact reports test-set metrics, or explicitly justify CV-only evaluation.

concerns.location: plan.md: Phase 7; research.md Methodology item 8; data-model.md 'Embeddings'
concerns.text: Interpretability analysis unit-of-analysis is ambiguous. Node embeddings are per-element-per-material ('[n_elements, hidden_dim]' in data-model.md suggests one row per element occurrence), but the correlated external properties (thermal conductivity, sound velocity, first ionization energy) are per-element scalars. The plan never states how embeddings are aggregated to the element level (mean over materials? final fold only?) nor the effective sample size (number of distinct elements, likely <100, possibly <50 after cleaning). Pearson p-values and Bonferroni correction depend on this N; without specifying the aggregation and N, SC-005's p<0.05 threshold is not well-defined. Specify the aggregation rule and the sample unit.

The 'corrected resampled t-test style' paired fold comparison is named but the correction (Nadeau-Bengio correction factor?) and the exact statistic are not specified; with 5 folds this choice materially changes the p-value. Name the specific test formula or cite the correction so the implementation is deterministic.

FR-005/FR-011 (CIF retrieval via MP REST API) and SC-002 (ΔR² information loss) have no executable plan element — Phase 8 is a code-path stub only and the plan itself states 'No scientific structure-aware run is claimed.' The spec's Assumptions ('MP Open Data is accessible... pipeline will automatically download missing CIFs') contradict the plan's finding that the API is credential-gated. Spec must be revised (re-scope or supply an open CIF source) before these FRs/SC are coverable.

Plan Phase 2 uses a 5-feature node list including element fraction; spec FR-002 mandates exactly [atomic number, electronegativity, valence electrons, atomic radius]. The plan flags this as kickback item 3, but as written the plan element does not match the FR — spec FR-002 must be amended (the plan's FeO≡Fe2O3 argument is sound).

FR-006 requires ΔR² = R²_composition − R²_structure-aware on a shared test set; the plan's Phase 6 delivers only a GNN-vs-RF 'delta_vs_rf' baseline gap via 5-fold CV, explicitly 'NOT a structure information-loss metric.' The FR's core clause is unbacked by any plan element; spec revision (plan's kickback item 2) must land.

FR-007 specifies '95% confidence intervals for predictions as mean ± 1.96 × std'; the plan relabels this a fold-disagreement band (kickback item 4). Plan element and FR wording disagree — spec wording must be revised to match the delivered semantics.

All success criteria are non-computable under the current plan (no verified dataset with formula/band_gap/hardness/crystal_system; hardness provenance unverified per reviewer). The plan transparently gates the scientific run, but the spec's Assumptions ('hardness values are derived from DFT... sufficient consistency') are unverified. Spec must either attach a verified conforming dataset or re-scope the targets.

The interpretability phase correlates PCs with thermal conductivity, sound velocity, and first ionization energy, but no source for this elemental-property lookup table is named anywhere (plan, research, or data-model). Unlike the main dataset, this resource is NOT flagged as unavailable and NOT covered by the data contract. Name the intended source (e.g. pymatgen's periodic-table data, a specific open elemental-properties table) or add it to the gated/limitations list so it cannot silently become an invented table at implementation time.

concerns.location: plan.md:Constitution Check / Principle VI; constitution.md:Principle VI
concerns.text: The plan, spec, and constitution remain mutually incompatible as written: Principle VI mandates a structure-aware comparison for EVERY reported evaluation metric, while the plan delivers composition-only metrics (Phase 6, results_composition_only.json) with the structure-aware path deferred (Phase 8, code-path stub only). The plan honestly flags this and requests an amendment, but until the kickback lands, any metrics artifact produced by this plan violates the constitution. The spec/constitution revision must be resolved before task generation, not after.

concerns.location: data-model.md:Metrics JSON ('Per-fold detail included') vs contracts/model_metrics.schema.yaml
concerns.text: data-model.md states the metrics JSON includes 'Per-fold detail', but model_metrics.schema.yaml sets additionalProperties: false at the top level and defines no per-fold field (only *_mean/*_std aggregates). Either add a per-fold block to the schema or remove the claim from data-model.md — as written, a conforming artifact cannot contain per-fold detail.

concerns.location: plan.md:Phase 6 vs Summary ('never reported as study results')
concerns.text: Phase 6 (marked 'gated; fixture run now') trains on tiny_materials.csv and emits data/results_composition_only.json — the same SSoT artifact named for scientific results. The plan promises fixture values are 'used only for software validation, never reported as study results', but does not specify how fixture-run outputs are distinguished (separate path, label field, or overwrite-on-data-arrival). Specify the mechanism so fixture metrics cannot be mistaken for the scientific SSoT artifact.

concerns.location: plan.md:Spec deviations (FR-002, FR-006, FR-007) vs spec.md
concerns.text: Three deliberate deviations from spec FRs (5-feature node list vs FR-002's 4; 5-fold CV means vs FR-006's shared test set; fold-disagreement band vs FR-007's '95% CI') are consistently documented across plan/research/data-model, but the spec text is unchanged. These are cross-doc disagreements that must be resolved by the requested spec revision before tasks are generated against the deviating definitions.

concerns.location: plan.md Phase 1 / research.md Methodology step 1 — 'rows outside 1.5×IQR of either target are dropped'
concerns.text: Applying a 1.5×IQR filter to the TARGET variables (band_gap, hardness) before training truncates the genuine heavy-tailed distribution of materials properties (wide-gap insulators, ultrahard compounds are real, not outliers). This systematically biases R²/MAE upward and makes the evaluation non-representative of the population the model claims to predict. Outlier filtering on targets is not standard practice in materials ML; if retained at all, it should be justified or restricted to clearly erroneous values, and the fraction dropped per target reported alongside metrics.

concerns.location: plan.md Phase 7 / research.md Methodology step 8 — interpretability property list 'thermal conductivity, sound velocity, first ionization energy'
concerns.text: First ionization energy is strongly correlated with electronegativity (an input node feature; r ≈ 0.9 across elements), so a significant PC–ionization correlation is partially circular in the same way the plan already excludes atomic mass and bulk modulus. Either exclude ionization energy, or report its correlation with the input features so readers can judge the circularity; the current exclusion list is inconsistent.

concerns.location: plan.md Phase 6 — 'Train GNN + RF per fold on the fixture (scientific run gated)'
concerns.text: Phase 6 will emit data/results_composition_only.json from the ~20-row fixture. The plan states fixture results are 'never reported as study results', but the metrics artifact path and schema are identical to the scientific one. Add an explicit provenance field (e.g. dataset_checksum already exists — state that fixture-derived artifacts must be marked as such / segregated) so a fixture-derived metrics JSON cannot be mistaken for a scientific result downstream.
